subject: Field masking and retention cutoff options for PHI
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@northstarhealth.org>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T17:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on field masking / retention limits for PHI

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking the time. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will ingest downstream patient intake and claims data. A few compliance questions from our security and privacy teams before we proceed:

1) Can Redwood enforce per-field retention limits (e.g., keep clinical notes for 7 years, but SSNs only 90 days) and automatically purge according to those schedules?
2) For regulated PHI, what are our redaction options? Do you support field-level masking (irreversible transform), reversible tokenization, and full deletion? What's the recommended approach if we need to retain some analytical signal but remove direct identifiers?
3) For deletion requests (subject erasure), can Redwood provide a signed certificate of deletion and associated audit log evidence showing which objects were removed and when?
4) If we opt for Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), are deletion/retention guarantees different vs Hosted? Any limitations for cross-region data residency?

Attached a small schema sample that shows the fields we'd like to treat differently. Also include the CISO's note about wanting a timeline for a bulk purge of ~50k patient records if we need to run a one-off erasure.

Attachments: northstar_schema_sample.csv (CSV, ~8KB)

Would appreciate a short playbook / options matrix we can share with security.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Security & Privacy
NorthStar Health
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@northstarhealth.org>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on field masking / retention limits for PHI

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the schema. I've summarized our options below and added Grace (legal) and Diego (infra) to clarify contractual and technical details. Quick answers up front: yes, per-field retention and multiple redaction strategies are supported; the implementation and evidence we provide depend on deployment mode and your contractual needs.

High-level options (recommendation at the end):

A) Field-level irreversible masking (recommended for direct identifiers you never need again)
  - Description: deterministic irreversible hash or cryptographic salt + truncation. No reversible mapping kept by default.
  - Use-case: SSN, government IDs, free-text PHI you want scrubbed.
  - Evidence: audit trail records delete/transform job details and storage objects modified; we can provide export showing transformation hashes.

B) Tokenization (reversible, controlled)
  - Description: replace original value with a token; mapping stored in a customer-managed key vault (recommended for Private deployments).
  - Use-case: when you need to rehydrate for clinical workflows under strict access controls.
  - Evidence: tokenization logs + access logs; requires KMS/HSM integration for key management.

C) Full deletion / erasure
  - Description: permanent removal from primary store(s) and scheduled removal from backups according to retention windows.
  - Caveat: backups & replicas have retention windows — we support accelerated purge for backups in Dedicated/Private but Hosted customers have standard recovery window unless contractually agreed.

Retention mechanics:
  - Per-field TTL: yes, you can configure retention rules per-field or per-entity type. Rules are enforced by our async purge pipeline.
  - Cutoff vs soft-delete: we support soft-delete flags for reversibility during dispute windows; final erasure runs as scheduled job.
  - SLA / timeline: for a one-off bulk purge of ~50k records we typically schedule a purge job that completes within 24–72 hours depending on region and whether data is archived. We can provide tighter timelines under Dedicated/Private with committed capacity.

Evidence and auditability:
  - We provide an audit bundle: job id, timestamps, object keys, counts removed/masked, and sha256 digests where applicable. For Hosted plans this is delivered as a signed report; for Private, you control the signing key.

Deployment differences:
  - Hosted: we can enforce per-field TTLs and run purge jobs, but backup snapshots may persist for the snapshot retention period (we can contract accelerated backups purge for enterprise deals).
  - Dedicated/Private: more control — you can request immediate backup purge or bring your own key management; we can provide deletion certificates signed by customer key.

Attachments I've included: SOC2-Summary.pdf (short summary of controls) and redwood-data-lifecycle-v2.docx (playbook + examples). See linked HubSpot record for the pilot.

Recommendation: For NorthStar pilot, start with irreversible masking for SSN/insurance_number + tokenization for identifiers you may need to rehydrate (store tokens in your KMS). Configure per-field TTLs for notes vs identifiers and request an accelerated purge SLA in the contract to cover backups.

Next steps: Grace will flag any contract language; Diego will open an INFRA ticket to scope the purge job and ETA. If you can share the expected retention windows per field (a table), we can draft a short SOW and timeline.

— Jasmine
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — looping in a couple of contractual notes from the legal perspective:

1) DPA language: we'll include explicit retention cutoffs and an accelerated backups purge clause if NorthStar needs deletion certificates within X days. Please confirm desired timeframes; Grace suggests 30/90/365 days as examples in the SOW.
2) Evidence: we can provide a signed deletion certificate plus the audit bundle Jasmine described. For Hosted, the certificate will be signed by Redwood; for Private, we can sign using customer-provided key material.
3) Regulatory note: when you request erasure of PHI, please specify whether you want irreversible masking for specific fields vs full record deletion — the latter may impact analytics and downstream reconciliation.

I've drafted a short DPA change request and uploaded to DocuSign for review: https://docusign.net/DocuSignEnvelope12345

If NorthStar requires HIPAA-specific attestations beyond SOC 2 (e.g., BAAs), let us know and we'll route to the partnerships team for BAA onboarding.

Subject: Re: Questions on field masking / retention limits for PHI

Hey all — technical addendum on purge mechanics and options from infra:

1) Implementation patterns:
   - Inline transform: apply masking/tokenization at ingestion. Best for minimizing storage of raw PHI.
   - Post-hoc purge job: runs against object store and DB to remove or transform fields. Good for retroactive requests.

2) Backups & replicas:
   - Hosted: snapshot retention is 30–90d depending on plan. We can add an accelerated purge to the contract; otherwise snapshots will respect the retention policy.
   - Dedicated/Private: we can configure snapshot lifecycles or provide tooling to purge snapshots.

3) Performance / timeline estimates:
   - One-off bulk purge of 50k records (typical 15 fields each): estimated wall time 8–36 hours on Dedicated capacity, 24–72 hours on Hosted depending on queue and region. We'll allocate an ops window to avoid interfering with production traffic.
   - We will produce an operation id (op-INFRA-####) and daily progress report; final bundle includes counts/sha256 digests and object keys.

4) Audit log outputs:
   - Logs include: job_id, timestamp, target_selector (customer_id + field list), objects_scanned, objects_modified, error_count, and exporter file location (S3 link).

I've created a tracking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2345 — will annotate with expected start date once NorthStar confirms timeframe.

— Diego
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Can you provide an SOW with the accelerated purge SLA and a price for the accelerated backups purge? We'll need the one-off purge completed by 2027-01-31 if possible.
- Please run a test purge on a 500-record sandbox to validate process and provide the audit bundle.
